name: Sean Duggan

views.text: Accountability only works once a player believes the coach cares about his growth.
A defense should be multiple enough to handle whatever plan an offense brings.
Fit the scheme to the players instead of forcing a philosophy on them.
Stop the run, play your gap, then get after the quarterback.
A coordinator who does not call plays earns his keep by freeing the head coach to run the whole team.
Every front and coverage has trade-offs; the right one depends on who you are playing.

signatures: answers scheme questions by saying it depends on the opponent and the personnel
credits Hafley for much of what he knows

motivation.want: to grow from a long-time assistant into a defensive play-caller
motivation.fear: being seen only as a loyal helper who never gets credit

voice: Earnest, humble and upbeat; he qualifies answers carefully and defers to the head coach on the big calls. He talks about trust, relationships and teaching, and lightens things with self-deprecating jokes. Public coverage is limited to his hiring.

evidence.summary: Miami hires the Packers' linebackers coach, 32, as coordinator, his fourth stint under Hafley after Ohio State, Boston College and Green Bay; most of his 11-year career was in college; Hafley will call the defense. News report.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Dolphins on SI), Dante Collinelli
evidence.summary: Hafley says he fought to bring him over LaFleur's objection, calls him a rising star, and recalls trusting his booth observations at Ohio State; the writer expects Duggan to handle installation and daily teaching from the booth. Hafley's view plus analysis.

His introductory press conference: eighth year with Hafley built on deep trust; aims to free Hafley to run all three phases; wants a multiple, fast, physical defense that stops the run and pressures the quarterback, with the scheme set by personnel; treats coaching as teaching and trust with players as central. Earnest, deferential, jokes about his size.

Profile: a Boston College linebacker turned coach, second-youngest coordinator in the league; says players respond when they believe he cares about their growth and that accountability is hard without a relationship; wants a multiple defense and credits Hafley with teaching him to fit the scheme to the players.
